title: Explain Client-Side Image Mapping in HTML5
summaryPoint: Mapping clickable hotspot regions on a single image linked to different URLs using <map> and <area> tags.
keyPoints: Client-side image mapping is defined using the tag with a mandatory name attribute linked to an image via the usemap="#mapname" attribute in .
The <area> tag is placed inside <map> to define specific clickable coordinate shapes: rect (rectangle), circle, and poly (polygon).
Key attributes of <area> include: shape, coords (coordinates for clickable area), href (target web URL), and alt (alternative text description).

title: Explain CSS3 Flexbox and its Container Properties
summaryPoint: Flexible Box Layout module for designing fluid, responsive layouts without complex floats or positioning.
keyPoints: A Flexbox layout is activated on a parent container by specifying display: flex; or display: inline-flex;.
flex-direction defines the main axis direction along which flex items are placed (row, row-reverse, column, column-reverse).
justify-content aligns items along the horizontal main axis (flex-start, flex-end, center, space-between, space-around).
align-items aligns items along the cross axis vertically (stretch, center, flex-start, flex-end).

title: Differentiate between Semantic and Non-Semantic Elements in HTML5
summaryPoint: Semantic elements clearly convey their meaning to both browser and developer, whereas non-semantic elements tell nothing about content.
keyPoints: Semantic Elements clearly define their purpose and structural role in a document structure. Examples: <header>, <nav>, <section>, <article>, <aside>, and <footer>.
Non-Semantic Elements tell nothing about the content they enclose and serve only as generic styling wrappers. Examples: <div> and <span>.
Using semantic tags improves SEO rankings, web accessibility (screen readers), and code maintainability.

title: Explain <audio> and <video> Elements in HTML5
summaryPoint: Native multimedia embedding tags eliminating the historical requirement for third-party flash plugins.
keyPoints: The <audio> tag embeds sound files (MP3, OGG, WAV) into a webpage without external plugins.
The <video> tag embeds video streams (MP4, WebM, OGG) directly in the browser layout.
Common attributes supported by both tags: src (source path), controls (displays play, pause, volume bar), autoplay (starts immediately), loop (replays continuously), and muted (mutes default audio).

title: Explain HTML5 Form Validation Attributes
summaryPoint: Built-in declarative validation rules executed by modern browsers before form submission without custom JavaScript.
keyPoints: required: Specifies that an input field cannot be left blank during submission.
pattern: Enforces a regular expression that the input field value must match (e.g. mobile or postal format).
placeholder: Displays temporary hint text inside the input box describing the expected input format.
min & max: Specifies minimum and maximum numerical or date limits for <input type="number"> or <input type="date">.
